stem: The leaves of many plants have stomata that show a regular daily rhythm of opening and closing over a period of 24 hours.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain why it is important for plants to open and close their stomata in a daily rhythm.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
Fig. 2.1 shows the results of an experiment to monitor this rhythm over three days and nights for the plant *Arabidopsis thaliana*. The percentage of open stomata is shown. Each day consisted of 14 hours of light (white bar) and each night consisted of 10 hours of darkness (black bar).

{{figure:figure_2_1.png}}
parts.text: Fig. 2.1 shows that the percentage of open stomata increases in the first seven hours of the experiment. Describe the sequence of changes that occurs in the guard cells that leads to the stomata opening.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem:
The experiment was repeated with *A. thaliana* plants that were left in darkness from 14 to 96 hours. The results are shown in Fig. 2.2.

{{figure:figure_2_2.png}}
parts.text: With reference to Fig. 2.1, explain what Fig. 2.2 shows about the role of genes and the role of the environment in controlling the rhythm of stomatal opening and closing in *A. thaliana*.
